newsitem.title: USA: AT&T Q2 in line with lowered expectations.
newsitem.headline: AT&T Q2 in line with lowered expectations.

text.p: AT&T Corp on Monday reported second quarter earnings substantially below a year ago but in line with Wall Street's severely lowered expectations, reflecting heavy investments the company is making to enter new markets.
AT&T reported earnings from continuing operations of $0.59 a share, a penny ahead of the First Call consensus estimate of $0.58.
Investments in growth markets like wireless, local phone service and the Internet diluted second quarter earnings by about $0.23 per share versus $0.16 a year ago, AT&T said.
Revenues from continuing operations in the quarter rose 2.4 percent, to $13.173 billion from $12.868 billion in the 1996 second quarter.
The revenue increase was driven by growth in business long-distance services, wireless services and AT&T Solutions, partially offset by declines in financial services revenues.

Core long-distance revenues for the quarter increased 1.5 percent, to $11.58 billion. Long-distance call volumes grew 9.7 percent from the 1996 second quarter but were down 0.5 percent from the first quarter of 1997.

The increased revenue-to-volume gap resulted from the continued effects of pricing pressures on new business contracts, changes in product mix, the use of free calling minutes as a customer retention tool, and the increased customer acceptance of calling plans, AT&T said.
Revenues from communications services rose 3 percent from a year ago, to $12.822 billion, in the second quarter.
Wireless revenues rose 14 percent, to $1.09 billion.
Financial services revenues declined 16.3 percent, to $351 million, primarily reflecting the impact of a securitization program at AT&T Universal Card Services.

"While we are making good progress against the commitments we made to our investors earlier this year, we're certainly not pleased with the year-over-year decline in our earnings," said AT&T Chairman Robert Allen.
"Our results reflect the short-term effect of our strategy to strengthen and grow the business over the long term," he said.

Allen said the company remains committed to delivering on its overall financial targets, "despite the fact that our local service efforts have been slowed by the foot-dragging of entrenched monopolies."

In March, AT&T said it expected 1997 full-year earnings from its core long-distance business of $3.45-$3.75 per share. It also said heavy investments in new markets were expected to cut those earnings by $0.75 to $1.00 a share.
Business long-distance revenues totalled $5.598 billion in the second quarter, up 4.1 percent from a year ago, driven by strong double-digit growth in data services.

Business volume growth, led by toll-free services, was in the mid-teens. The volume increase was almost entirely offset by the continued impact of lower prices in new contracts with business customers and a change in product mix.
Total cellular subscribers rose 22.1 percent to 7.6 million.
The cellular subscriber growth rate was hurt by the sale of several wireless properties in the 1996 fourth quarter.
Revenues from local and other initiatives increased $166 million in the second quarter to $524 million, a 46.5 percent gain from a year ago.
The category includes AT&T Solutions, its systems integration business, AT&T Worldnet and other online services, international expansion, and local service.
The AT&T Worldnet Internet access service ended the quarter with a subscriber base of about 923,000.
AT&T Worldnet subscriber growth was hurt by the discontinuance of the five-free-hours introductory plan.
Operating expenses increased 10.1 percent in the quarter to $11.614 billion.
The growth was led by increases in network and other communications services expenses as well as access and other interconnection expenses.

In addition, depreciation and amortization expenses rose $256 million, or 38.8 percent. Less than 20 percent of the increase related to new initiatives. The expense increase was driven principally by higher levels of capital spending.
Selling, general and administrative expenses were essentially flat with the year-ago quarter.
